content.title: Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special (TV Special 2026) ⭐ 6.6 | Documentary, Family, Music
content.text: Cast & crewUser reviewsTriviaTV Special20261hFollows Miley Cyrus in an interview with Alex Cooper, revisiting the moments, music and memories of Hannah Montana with never-before-seen archival footage and recreated sets from the show.Follows Miley Cyrus in an interview with Alex Cooper, revisiting the moments, music and memories of Hannah Montana with never-before-seen archival footage and recreated sets from the show.Follows Miley Cyrus in an interview with Alex Cooper, revisiting the moments, music and memories of Hannah Montana with never-before-seen archival footage and recreated sets from the show.34User reviews3Critic reviewsVideos2Featured reviewsA Self-Indulgent Nothing BurgerFor twenty years, I've been, not only a huge Hannah Montana fan but a huge Miley Cyrus fan. Unfortunately, I'm not one to say something is good just because I like the people involved in it.This felt self-indulgent, like a celebration of Miley rather than a celebration of the show itself. Not to say that Miley shouldn't be celebrated. I mean, she gave up a normal childhood so a generation of kids could have Hannah Montana as part of theirs. That is certainly worth celebrating. But what about the rest of the cast that helped make the show what it is? Where were they? I know damn well Jason Earles would have gladly been there.Billy Ray Cyrus was the only part of the main Hannah Montana cast that was actually there and it was very brief. He did not seem like he even wanted to be there.And what about the people that were behind the show, as well, who also made the show what it is? I'm sure they would've had a lot to say, and a lot of interesting stuff at that.Who they did have present was Miley's mother, Tish Cyrus. I understand that Tish played a big part in Miley getting the role of Hannah, and played a big part throughout Miley's career as Hannah, but Tish also did not bring much to this special besides her lovely accent and comments about Hannah's wardrobe.Alex Cooper was not a very good interviewer. Her questions were dull, generic, lacking in almost every sense and really didn't delve into any engaging topics. It would've been more fun and engaging to have someone who was part of the show do the interview.The Chappell Roan cameo was weird and completely unnecessary. That's all I have to say about that. Selena Gomez was a fine cameo, as she did have a small role in the show and it was nice to see her and Miley reminisce briefly, but cameos from people like Dolly Parton or David Koechner (Uncle Earl) or Francis Callier (Roxy like a puma!!!) would have been freakin' awesome! There are so many iconic recurring faces that Hannah Montana fans would've been so happy to see recount funny and exciting memories and talk about their time on the show. But no. I get people are busy and have schedules, but it doesn't even seem like the people who put this special together put in much effort at all.The best part of this in my opinion were, of course, Miley's performances. She has a beautiful singing voice and I'm so glad she's learned to love and appreciate Hannah Montana again.Overall, the Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special was a disappointing one that held no interest and did not live up to the warm feeling of nostalgia that the show brings to so many people. It just seemed rushed. Where were the never-before-seen clips? The deleted scenes? The behind-the-scenes stories? That would have been special.A Nostalgic Return That Fell a Bit ShortIt was refreshing to see Miley Cyrus step back into Hannah and perform a few songs-it definitely brought some nostalgia. That said, I was expecting a lot more from this special. I would've loved deeper behind-the-scenes moments from Hannah Montana, more storytelling from the cast, and longer, more meaningful conversations instead of quick "hi and goodbye" appearances.Overall, the special felt a bit rushed. For a 20th anniversary, I really expected something more in-depth and celebratory. Still, it's great to see Miley embracing Hannah as an important part of her journey.Where is the rest of the cast?I know the show was called Hannah Montana but why didn't we check in with the others. No Emily? No Jason? No Mitchel? Would love have loved to hear about their collective experience. Billy Ray Cyrus was there for a moment which was nice. That man was a good method actor. While filming the show, he spent 5 years being a dad to a pop star and never broke character.Just felt very oddThe fact that there was only a select few people invited to return was just very odd for an anniversary special.The special had more of Miley and Tish Cyrus than any of the cast or crew. The last seconds when her sister just suddenly appeared just summed up this was all about them rather than the show.The script read with Billy Ray was the highlight of special. I had a glimmer of hope Jason Earles was going to appear when he mentioned Jackson when leaving. The Selena Gomez section was a close second and shows how anniversary specials should blend the clips with the present day. You had plenty of other cast and disney guest you could have brought in but that wasn't the aim for their special.The host was very bland and only there to provide a resemblance of an anniversary special. The Chappell Roan interview was just to pull in modern viewers but what they discussed was Miley post Hannah Montana...Very blandChappell being there was odd, you can tell they only cared about how things looked. I've watched her since I was a little girl and I'm disappointed. I wasn't expecting things being so awkward. For it being a 20th special, it's not special. It ended up becoming background noise and really wish they gave us more then one on one talks and random music videos.More like thisRelated interestsContribute to this pageSuggest an edit or add missing contentEdit pageMore to explore
